provenance.citation: 26 U.S.C. Sec. 401(a)(9)(C)(v) (added by SECURE 2.0 Act of 2022, Pub. L. 117-328, div. T, title I, Sec. 107)
provenance.pin_status: Statutory pin retrieved and verified. The REGULATORY pin resolving the 1959-cohort overlap is VERIFY -- not retrieved.
provenance.authority_note: Retrieved text of 26 U.S.C. Sec. 401(a)(9)(C)(v): "(I) In the case of an individual who attains age 72 after December 31, 2022, and age 73 before January 1, 2033, the applicable age is 73. (II) In the case of an individual who attains age 74 after December 31, 2032, the applicable age is 75." THESE TWO CLAUSES OVERLAP: a person born in 1959 attains age 73 in 2032 (before Jan. 1, 2033, so clause (I) reaches them) and attains age 74 in 2033 (after Dec. 31, 2032, so clause (II) reaches them too). That is a drafting defect in SECURE 2.0 Sec. 107, not an ambiguity this record may resolve. The expression's clean 1960 split follows the administrative resolution adopted in Treasury's regulations under Sec. 401(a)(9) -- applicable age 73 for pre-1960 cohorts, 75 for 1960 and later. THAT REGULATORY PIN WAS NOT RETRIEVED THIS SESSION and is flagged VERIFY. The reference engine's formula encoded this interpretive choice as if it were bare statute; this note is the seam made visible.
